description:
2026-09-11. crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs:462 graphite_htr10_temperature_points FAILS: sigma_inel(393.15 K, 0.0253 eV) = 0.6797 b, pinned at 0.6779 b, gate 5e-4. Off by 0.27%.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED TODAY. Measured at three commits: fails at e71405d2 (BEFORE the wave-7 merge), at 0dc3e456 (the merge), and at HEAD. origin/develop is therefore ALREADY RED on outram-mc-libs and has been for at least the wave-5/6/7 window.

HOW IT WENT UNNOTICED: the verification loop this session ran 'cargo test -p njoy-outram-park-fork' only. outram-mc-libs consumes njoy's reconstruction and asserts on it, so a njoy data change can break it while the njoy suite stays green. I merged wave 7 on a njoy-only green. That is a process gap, not a one-off.

WHAT THE VALUE IS. The test's own header records item 8 under 'Measured:' - these are REGRESSION PINS OF OUR OWN OUTPUT, not NJOY oracle values. So the workspace rule 'NJOY-listed sigma values must be UNCHANGED' does not apply, and updating the number is not automatically weakening an oracle. But the converse also holds: WITHOUT AN ORACLE I CANNOT SAY WHETHER 0.6797 IS BETTER OR WORSE THAN 0.6779. A self-pin detects change and is silent on correctness.

Only the 393.15 K row fails and only its sigma_inel; sigma_el at the same T passes (4.3849). 393.15 K is INTERPOLATED between tabulated 296 and 400 K. 523.15 and 1073.15 K are also interpolated but the loop panics before reaching them, so their status is UNKNOWN, not passing. Plausible cause: the thermal temperature-interpolation work in waves 5/6/7 (op-1y4y / op-cjw.22 touch exactly this surface).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: I did not update the pin to 0.6797. That would convert an unexplained change into a recorded fact.

TO CLOSE: run NJOY2016 THERMR on tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT 30) at 393.15 K and read sigma_inel at 0.0253 eV. The oracle binary is built in-session at crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/upstream_source/NJOY2016/build/njoy (never rebuild it). If NJOY gives 0.6797 the pin is stale and should be updated WITH that citation; if it gives 0.6779 this is a regression in the interpolation and the njoy change is at fault. Then re-enable the loop past 393.15 K and check 523.15 and 1073.15 too.

ALSO WORTH FIXING: the verification command must cover the whole workspace, or at least outram-mc-libs alongside njoy, before any njoy merge.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 FIXED on develop 0472ef37. The pin was wrong, and the OLD value came from a demonstrably broken interpolation — established by measurement, not by picking whichever number was newer.

WHAT MOVED. Probed both checkouts on the byte-identical tape: every TABULATED temperature unchanged (296 K 0.486340, 400 K 0.695883, 500 K 0.902683) and sigma_el unchanged EVERYWHERE, while every INTERPOLATED temperature moved. Signature of an interpolation change, not a data change.

WHY THE NEW VALUES ARE RIGHT. sigma_inel rises monotonically with T, so a request strictly between two tabulated temperatures MUST give a cross section between the two tabulated cross sections. Physical bound, not a tolerance. The pre-op-55lj interpolation broke it, measured at 393.15 K bracketed by 296/400 K:
    1.0 eV  4.262049  4.296979  4.366657  inside
    2.0 eV  4.497721  4.429965  4.550130  OUTSIDE by -1.51%
    3.9 eV  4.609533  4.417445  4.636609  OUTSIDE by -4.17%
Cause: it interpolated S(alpha,beta) point-by-point at fixed (alpha,beta) then integrated with the TARGET temperature's kinematics; LAT=1 scales alpha,beta with 1/kT, so that mixes one temperature's law with another's kinematics. Current code evaluates kernel and sigma_inel consistently at each bracketing temperature and interpolates the RESULTS — verified at 0.00% excess across three brackets and five energies.

ON THE 'GET AN NJOY ORACLE' PLAN IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION: not possible, and that is not a testing gap. thermr.f90:347-349 errors 'desired temperature not on tape' unless the request is within 1e-4 of a tabulated value, and calcem does the same at :1720-1741 — UPSTREAM NEVER INTERPOLATES IN TEMPERATURE AT ALL. NJOY users LEAPR the exact temperature. Our interpolation is this port's ENDF-sanctioned generalisation, justified by the file's own LI=4 law. So the oracle here is the physical bracket, not NJOY.

Three interpolated sigma_inel updated (0.6779->0.6797, 0.9445->0.9471, 2.0373->2.0444); tabulated rows untouched.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBERS, and the reason I did not simply re-pin: a pinned value could not catch this. Item 8 samples only 0.0253 eV, where the violation does not appear, so it passed for weeks on a cross section 4% outside a physical bound at 3.9 eV. New test interpolated_sigma_inel_stays_inside_its_bracket asserts the bound over three brackets and five energies with floating-point slack only. A pin detects change; an invariant detects wrongness.

Side effect: the old failure aborted the loop at 393.15 K, so the 523.15 and 1073.15 rows had NEVER executed. They run now.

outram-mc-libs: 312 passed, 0 failed, 14 ignored, 8 binaries. develop is green.

title: outram-mc RED: graphite sigma_inel(393.15 K) self-pin broken by the njoy thermal work
